answer: The answer is committed as a 139 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. Because the comet commitment is timestamped in the yarrow ledger, the karst audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. Bonded capital sits idle for 15 days. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
